newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LANGER WANTS FAIRER SHARE-OUT OF RYDER PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER WANTS FAIRER SHARE-OUT OF RYDER PROFITS.

text.p: Bernhard Langer on Wednesday called for Europe's Ryder Cup players to be paid and also for there to be a fairer distribution of the profits from the bi-annual competition against the United States.

Langer, 39-year-old German veteran of the last eight European Ryder Cup teams and an almost certain member of the next one in September, said while it was a thrill to play in the tournament he disagreed with the present system.

"We've never been paid but maybe we should adopt something like the Americans and pay a few thousand dollars to cover expenses. On our Tour we all agreed not to be paid and half of the money goes back into our Tour and is used for good purposes," he said.
"The one thing I disagree with is that the British PGA gets the other half of the money and the German, Swedish and Irish PGAs get nothing.
"I don't agree with that at all. Ever since continental players became part of the Ryder Cup, part of the money should go to other PGAs."
Langer, winner of last week's Italian Open and currently lying sixth in the Ryder Cup standings, said he had already recommended to officials that changes should be made.
"They might listen, but it doesn't mean they will change. It's been mentioned before."
And he added: "It's not easy to convince them to give money away."
